phase: Phase 7 - Model Explainability & Oceanographic Feature Attribution

surface_layer_10m.physical_mechanism: Direct radiative and turbulent air-sea heat exchange governs the mixed layer.

thermocline_layer_100m.physical_mechanism: Sea Level Anomaly reflects vertical displacement of the main pycnocline and thermocline induced by planetary waves and mesoscale eddies.

deep_water_layer_500m.physical_mechanism: Thermal structure is decoupled from synoptic surface conditions and governed by basin-scale climatology and intermediate water mass distribution (Red Sea / Persian Gulf outflow vs Bay of Bengal low-salinity intermediate waters).

model_comparison_p5_vs_p6.summary: Phase 6 hyperparameter tuning and VotingRegressor ensembles improved physical fidelity, notably amplifying SLA sensitivity in the thermocline (75-125m) where vertical thermal gradients are steepest.

limitations: Small sample size of 75 collocated profiles across 13 Argo floats limits generalization to extreme anomalous years (e.g. strong IOD or ENSO events).
Spatial clustering of float trajectories in the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal may inflate the attribution of geographic coordinates (latitude, longitude) at deep levels.
Satellite current velocities (sat_current_u, sat_current_v) exhibited low relative attribution (<5%) due to smooth 0.25° gridding damping sub-mesoscale shear.
